transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I'm a high school teacher, and lately I just can't stop seeing this crooked, swollen-looking side of my face on our lesson videos. It's really getting to me. Once I notice it, I just feel like the students, their parents, the other staff... I feel like they must all be staring at it instead of actually listening to anything I'm saying.
Do you think your face really is noticeably deformed, or is part of you aware that it may just look that way to you?

I honestly don't know. I mean... when I look at those videos, it looks completely real and obvious to me. It's just right there. But I guess... I don't know if it's actually as bad to everyone else as it is to me, or if I'm just hyper-focused on it. It's hard to tell what other people are actually seeing. I just know what I see, and to me, it really does look deformed.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your face in mirrors or on camera because of this?

Yeah, I do. Especially on camera. Before I post a recorded lesson, or... or even before I join a parent conference online, I just can't leave it alone. 

I keep changing the camera angle, replaying the clips, trying to cover parts of my face with my hand to see if that helps hide it. Sometimes I end up re-recording the whole lesson so many times that I completely miss my prep work. I've actually ended up being late with my classes because I'm just stuck doing this over and over.
Has anyone you trust told you that your face looks normal?

Not really, no. Um... I haven't actually brought it up to anyone. I guess I'm just too embarrassed to ask my friends or family if they see what I see. So... no one has told me it looks normal, but I haven't exactly asked them about it, either.
Are you completely certain that this facial deformity is real?

I... I guess I can't say I'm one hundred percent certain, no. Like I was saying earlier, I haven't actually asked anyone else to verify it. 

But... it feels completely real to me. When I look at myself on the screen, it's just so obvious. So even if I try to tell myself that maybe it's not as bad as I think, I still see it right there. It's hard to convince myself it isn't real when I'm looking right at it.
If your face looked completely normal to you, would you still feel very anxious about being seen or judged by students, parents, or coworkers?

I don't think so. I mean, if I didn't see this... this issue with my face, I wouldn't have any reason to worry about them looking at me. 

Before this started bothering me so much, I was completely fine teaching, talking to parents, being on camera. It's really just this specific thing about how my face looks that makes me so anxious. If that were gone, I'd just be focused on my job again.
Besides checking your face on camera or replaying videos, do you get unwanted thoughts about your face that make you feel driven to do any other repeated rituals in your mind or behavior?

Yes, it's actually become a huge problem with my teaching. Um... before I post a recorded lesson or even join a parent conference, I get so caught up in how I look. I keep changing the camera angle, trying to find a way to hide it. I end up replaying clips over and over, sometimes just covering parts of my face with my hand to see if that helps. 

I'll re-record a whole lesson so many times that I completely miss my prep period. It's gotten to the point where I'm actually running late with my classes because I can't stop checking and re-doing it.
Have you seen a doctor about this facial problem?

No, I haven't seen a doctor about it. I mean, like a medical doctor or a plastic surgeon... no. I haven't talked to anyone about it until now. I guess I've just been trying to fix it or hide it on my own with the camera angles and everything. I haven't taken that step to actually go to a professional to look at my face.
Are you also afraid that people will judge you for things other than how your face looks?

No, not really. I mean, I know I'm a good teacher, and I've always gotten along well with the staff and the parents. I don't worry about them judging my teaching or my personality or anything like that. It really all just comes back to my face. If it weren't for how I look, I wouldn't be worried about their judgment at all.
Do you have repeated unwanted thoughts or rituals about things other than your face or appearance?

No, I don't think so. It's really just... just my face. I don't have any other things I feel like I have to do over and over, if that's what you mean. My mind is pretty much just entirely stuck on how I look.
